standard_prerequisites.name: Faithful flatness and weak etaleness of products of localizations

core_obligations: Form an auxiliary map (proof lines 2289-2296): given a weakly etale faithfully flat map A_Z^tilde -> B, consider the ring map from A to the product of the localizations A_{f_i} and B; this map is faithfully flat and weakly etale.

Use w-contractibility (proof lines 2296-2300): since A is w-contractible there is a retraction sigma of that map, which yields a morphism from Spec(A_Z^tilde) into the disjoint union of the spectra of the A_{f_i} and of Spec(B).

Produce the retraction of the original map (proof lines 2300-2304): every point of Z lies in Spec(A_Z^tilde) and maps into the component Spec(B), and since every point of Spec(A_Z^tilde) specializes to a point of Z, the image of Spec(A_Z^tilde) lies in Spec(B); hence there is a morphism Spec(A_Z^tilde) -> Spec(B) over Spec(A_Z^tilde), which is the required retraction and proves that A_Z^tilde is w-contractible.
proof_roadmap: Enlarge the given weakly etale faithfully flat map by the localizations at the f_i so that w-contractibility of A applies.
Take a retraction and locate its image using that the points of Z map into the extra component.
Use the specialization property to conclude that the image lies in the intended component, giving the retraction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a closed subset Z of the spectrum of A of the form V(f_1, ..., f_r), if A is w-contractible then so is the localization A_Z^tilde (statement lines 2282-2287). The proof (proof lines 2289-2305) extends a given weakly etale faithfully flat map by the localizations at the f_i, takes a retraction using w-contractibility of A, and uses the specialization property of A_Z^tilde to conclude that the image lies in the intended component. H2: a three-step argument with two inputs, written out in full.
